rationale: The student added 7 + 6 to get 13 and wrote '13' directly next to the tens sum 5, failing to regroup the ten. Demonstrating 'place-value / make-a-ten' shows how a collection of ones greater than 9 bundles into 1 ten and leftover ones.
intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [15]. Tutor points at: 10 ones bundling into 1 ten

frames.caption: Here are 15 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 5 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 5 in the ones place: 15. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote '513' because they placed all 13 ones into the ones column instead of regrouping 10 ones into 1 ten. The demo directly targets this conceptual obstacle by showing 15 ones, explicitly stating that a place can only hold 0 to 9, bundling 10 ones into 1 ten, and showing that each place gets only one digit.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this demo clearly isolates and explains why a place column cannot hold two digits and demonstrates how 10 ones become 1 ten.
